key_insight: The paper generalizes thermodynamic dislocation theory to arbitrary macroscopic stress/strain states by averaging slip-system responses, yielding an associated J2 plasticity law with physics-based hardening.
engineering_relevance: It provides a single constitutive framework that can predict tension, compression, and torsion of copper across wide temperatures and strain rates without separately fitting each loading mode.
method: Use equal-probability grain orientation averaging to compute mean resolved shear stress and mean shear strains.
Apply exact isotropic orientation identities to connect averaged slip response to von Mises stress and the stress deviator.
Embed thermally activated dislocation depinning plus dislocation-density/effective-temperature evolution in time-rate form for arbitrary paths.
evidence_signal: The model was calibrated against 142 data points spanning Hopkinson-bar tension, dynamic compression, and torque-twist tests, matching results within about 6% rms.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the assumed initial dislocation state and can affect torsion predictions, so specimen history must be characterized carefully.
paper_title: Averaging in thermodynamic dislocation theory: general macroscopically uniform stress and strain states
